## Details

### `show sys-info`

```
show sys-info
show sys-info temperature
show sys-info fan
```

Sub-options bmc, card, cpld, fan, led, power, ssd, temperature, uboot and usb depend on the platform.


### `show software [detail]`

The first thing to check before and after an upgrade.


### `show running-config [module <module>]`

```
show running-config module isis
show running-config module i-sid
show running-config module mlt
```

A module is much faster to read than the full config. Some features have no module of their own (SNMP lines are in `module sys`, Extreme KB 000115014); for those, filter with `| include` (`ncs -t output-filters`). Use `show running-config verbose` to include default values.


### `show running-config verbose`

Use it when a default value is the suspect, e.g. timers or MTU.


### `save config [file <name>] [backup <name>]`

```
save config
save config file /intflash/pre-change_2026-10-12.cfg
```

Before a risky change, save a named copy. You can then compare with `more` or roll back with `boot config <file>`.


### `copy <source> <destination> [-y]`

```
copy /intflash/config.cfg /intflash/config_backup.cfg
copy /intflash/config.cfg 192.0.2.10:sw-core-01.cfg
```


### `dir [-l] [-r] [<path>]`

```
dir
dir /intflash/release/
```


### `more <file>`

```
more /intflash/config.cfg
```


### `grep <pattern> <file>`

```
grep "i-sid" /intflash/config.cfg
```


### `show boot config flags`

Many features (MACsec, DvR leaf, VRF scaling) only work with the right boot flag set. A changed flag only takes effect after save config and a reboot.


### `boot config choice primary config-file <file>`

```
boot config choice primary config-file /intflash/pre-change_2026-10-12.cfg
```

Together with a named backup file, this gives you a clean rollback path.


### `software add <file>.voss`

```
software add 5520.9.4.2.0.voss
show software
```

Upload the image first, by USB or by SFTP (needs boot flag sshd) / FTP (needs ftpd). The image file is deleted after unpacking. The 4220, 5320 and 5420 Series keep at most two releases, so the non-primary one is overwritten.


### `software activate <release>`

```
show software
software activate 9.4.2.0.GA
save config
reset -y
```

> ▲ **Caution:** The switch needs a reboot afterwards. Plan a maintenance window.


### `software commit`

By default `sys software auto-commit` is enabled, so the switch commits on its own when the timer (`sys software commit-time`, default 10 minutes) expires. Commit manually to end the timer early. For a real safety net, disable auto-commit before the upgrade: if the new release breaks management access and nobody commits, the switch reboots into the previous release.


### `no sys software auto-commit enable`

```
no sys software auto-commit enable
sys software commit-time 20
```

> ▲ **Caution:** With auto-commit off, a forgotten `software commit` reboots the switch into the old release.


### `reset -in <[d:][hh:]mm>`

```
reset -in 15
! ... do the change, verify it works, then:
reset -cancel
```

VOSS has no "commit confirmed". If you lock yourself out, the switch reboots after the timer and loads the saved (unchanged) config. Do not save config until the change is verified, then cancel the reset. Hours and minutes need two digits, e.g. 1:30 means 1 h 30 min. The maximum is 9:23:59.

> ▲ **Caution:** If you forget `reset -cancel`, the switch reboots. Unsaved changes are lost.


### `reset -y`

> ▲ **Caution:** Traffic impact. Unsaved changes are lost.


### `show logging file [tail] [severity <sev>] [module <module>] [event-code <code>]`

```
show logging file tail
show logging file severity ERROR
show logging file tail | include ISIS
show logging file tail | include 1/12
```

Several values can be combined with a pipe, e.g. `severity ERROR|WARNING`.


### `show khi performance [cpu | memory | process sort <field> | pthread]`

```
show khi performance cpu
show khi performance memory
show khi performance pthread sort cpu
```

Run this first when the CLI is slow or protocols flap and a high CPU is suspected.


### `show khi resource-scaling`

Moved from Privileged EXEC to User EXEC in 9.4. Since 9.4 the switch logs a warning and raises an alarm at 80, 90 and 100 % usage.


### `show io resources <option>`

```
show io resources filter
```


### `show fulltech [khi] [file <file>]`

```
show fulltech file /intflash/fulltech_2026-10-12.txt
```

Since 9.2 it is only available in Privileged EXEC. Pipe filters such as include do not work with show fulltech. `show tech` is a shorter alias.


### `flight-recorder all 1`

Run it right after a crash or a strange event, before you reboot. The files go to /intflash.


### `show pluggable-optical-modules {basic | detail} [<port>]`

```
show pluggable-optical-modules basic
show pluggable-optical-modules detail 1/49
```

The first check for CRC errors or flapping fiber links. Rx power close to the low alarm threshold points to dirty connectors or a bad patch.


### `show license`

Premier is required for some features, e.g. Segmented VRF with an L3 VSN or more VRFs. Since 9.3.1 the output also shows Premier features included in Extreme Platform ONE licenses.


### `show ssh session`

Up to 9.2 this was a single `show ssh` command.


### `ssh <host | IS-IS hostname | system-id> -l <user>`

```
ssh SW-ACCESS-12 -l admin
```

Handy for jumping across the fabric to a switch whose management IP you don't know. Not possible to a boundary node from an IS-IS remote area.


### `ping <ip> [vrf <vrf>] [source <ip>] [count <n>] [datasize <bytes>] [-s]`

```
ping 10.10.20.1 vrf CORP
ping 10.10.20.1 vrf CORP source 10.10.10.1 count 100
ping 10.10.20.1 datasize 1472
ping 10.10.20.1 -s -I 1
```

Without `vrf`, the ping uses the GRT. `-s` pings continuously at the `-I` interval (stop with Ctrl+C). `mgmt clip|oob|vlan` pings from the segmented management instance.


### `traceroute <ip> [vrf <vrf>] [source <ip>]`

```
traceroute 10.10.20.1 vrf CORP
```

Inside the fabric, `l2 traceroute` shows the SPB hops. IP traceroute only shows the routed hops.


### `sys name <hostname>`

```
sys name SW-CORE-01
```

Set the IS-IS hostname separately with `sys-name` in IS-IS Router Config.


### `clilog enable`

Up to 9.3 the command was just `clilog`. Use `copy clilog <file>` to export the log.


### `show mgmt interface [clip | oob | vlan]`

```
show mgmt interface
show mgmt ip route
```


### `show sys mtu`

The default is 1950 bytes, which already covers the 22 bytes of SPB MAC-in-MAC overhead for standard 1500-byte frames. Set jumbo frames with `sys mtu <size>` (the range depends on the platform, see `sys mtu ?`) and keep the value the same on every switch in the fabric.


### `monitor ports statistics <ports> interface utilization`

```
monitor ports statistics 1/1-1/4 interface utilization
```

Set the refresh interval and duration with `monitor-statistics interval <sec>` and `monitor-statistics duration <sec>`.


### `monitor ports error <ports> main`

```
monitor ports error 1/12 main
```


### `show application iqagent status`

`show application iqagent` shows the agent settings (server, proxy).


### `show khi cpp port-statistics [<ports>]`

```
show khi cpp port-statistics 1/1-1/48
```

A port with a huge ARP, broadcast or IGMP count is usually the source (loop, scanner, misbehaving host). On an MLT the counters increase equally on all members.


### `trace level <module-id> <0-4> / trace screen enable / trace shutdown`

```
trace level 14 3
trace screen enable
trace shutdown
```

The module IDs differ per platform; use the CLI help (`trace level ?`). The official vIST troubleshooting procedure uses module 14 to watch ARP requests and replies, as in the example. Usually requested by Extreme GTAC.

> ▲ **Caution:** Verbose tracing can load the CPU. Always end with `trace shutdown`.
